status: design only; nothing launched; no model run by the designer
goal: An RL recipe started FROM I that beats its paired time-matched SFT-from-I control by >= +0.03 dev800 equal-class accuracy (paired bootstrap 95% LB > 0) and beats I by >= +0.03.
hard_rules: dev800 / h_select / h_gate_final / TRAIN only. Never native VAL or sealed TEST.

Every RL arm has a paired SFT-from-I control on the SAME host, launched right after it, time-matched at every RL checkpoint (stop-after-active-seconds = RL committed_active_seconds at that checkpoint).
Control label access = every row whose label the RL arm read (screened arms: every SCANNED row, not only accepted ones). Never more.
Selection fairness: RL and its control each get the same number of dev800 looks; the comparison uses best-of-k on both sides, then finalists are confirmed once on h_gate_final.
Commit raw summaries to docs/aircraft-rl-campaign-I/ before interpreting.

arms.branch: sweep-wave2-integration.noindex (screen from main lineage); runs on rl-campaign-base
arms.rationale: Online screen at u_8(p) >= 0.5 under the CURRENT policy removes the all-correct groups that were 48% of RL400 (193/400) and the p~0 groups; std-scaled GRPO weights mid-p images most; beta 0 drops the reference forward (~31% cheaper on 3070). Highest EV: attacks the measured dominant waste with existing code.

Partial credit gives signal on images where I is wrong but in the right family (the 737-500/600, E-190/195, Gulfstream IV/V confusions); invalid -0.5 turns the 38% format-only signal into a penalty on out-of-vocabulary strings rather than the only contrast; dynamic sampling redraws all-same groups. Unscreened, so it can run past 600.

Generation dominates CPU cost (G8 136 s vs SFT 11.5 s); reusing each group for 2 optimizer passes buys updates per second, which is exactly what the time-matched control punishes. Screening refuses with num_iterations>1, so dynamic sampling supplies the filter.
Half the cost of G8 per update, so ~2x the updates in the same seconds; the screen guarantees the group is still likely mixed. Tests whether update count beats group size under a time match.

Confuser-aware: -0.5 for a frozen-map confuser pushes down the model's own near-variant mode, the one thing SFT on gold cannot do directly. Confusion map came from W rollouts on S (TRAIN), no held-out labels.
Same as A01 with Dr-GRPO; its expected limit is band-masked CE weighted by 2p (docs/aircraft-rl-next-study-v1.md section 1), so A01 vs A06 tells whether std weighting toward mid-p matters from I.
RL400 barely moved (KL <= 0.0035 per window, every useful step clipped at norm 1); a higher LR is the direct test of under-movement.
GRPO-W at 1e-5 lost 7.1 pp vs I; from I the risk is forgetting, so the low end of the LR grid guards the downside.
Full DAPO recipe; clip-higher only binds when a batch is reused, hence num_iterations 2.

Static pool of images where I is mid-band OR wrong; hierarchical credit is the only reward that gives signal on I-wrong p~0 images, which the exact-p screen discards. Control trains on the same pool (its label access).

Every sampled answer valid, so every mixed group contrasts gold with a real confuser. Ranked mid because it needs new code with a bias risk and the validity headroom at I is only +1.2 pp; evaluated with the unconstrained greedy evaluator like every arm.
KL anchor to I; costs ~45% more seconds than A01, so the time-matched control gets more; tells whether anchoring to I is worth its price.
Less label smoothing than A02 (family credit 0.5 may reward stopping at the family); lower LR.
Conservative long-horizon arm: cheapest RL update, smallest LR, preserves I while accumulating hard-example signal.

arms.rationale: Expert iteration on prompts I does not already solve 8/8. Low EV against a gold-label SFT control (correct own samples are a subset of gold), but it is the cheapest per-update on-policy method and isolates on-policy-data value.
RFT LR and keep-count axis.
Static I-scored hard pool with exact reward and cycling: decomposes A01 (online screen) vs offline pool, and can go past 600.
